```json
{
  "tests": [
    {
      "name": "Happy path writes usage to writer",
      "given": "a valid io.Writer",
      "expect": "writes the formatted usage error to the writer and returns nil",
      "polarity": "success",
      "covers": "happy"
    },
    {
      "name": "Returns error when writing to the writer fails",
      "given": "an io.Writer that returns an error on Write",
      "expect": "returns the error from the writer",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "covers": "error:1"
    }
  ]
}
```

```go
package cli

import (
	"errors"
	"io"
	"testing"
)

type writeUsageErrorWriterErr struct{}

func (w writeUsageErrorWriterErr) Write(p []byte) (n int, err error) {
	return 0, errors.New("write failed")
}

func TestWriteUsageError(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		w       func() io.Writer
		wantErr bool
		errStr  string
	}{
		{
			name: "Happy path writes usage to writer",
			w: func() io.Writer {
				return new(bytes.Buffer)
			},
			wantErr: false,
		},
		{
			name: "Returns error when writing to the writer fails",
			w: func() io.Writer {
				return writeUsageErrorWriterErr{}
			},
			wantErr: true,
			errStr:  "write failed",
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var buf bytes.Buffer
			var w io.Writer
			if tt.w != nil {
				w = tt.w()
			} else {
				w = &buf
			}

			// Handle the error case where we don't want to capture buffer output
			// but we need to pass the writer.
			if tt.wantErr && tt.errStr != "" {
				// For the error case, we use the error-returning writer directly
				err := writeUsageError(tt.w())
				if err == nil || err.Error() != tt.errStr {
					t.Errorf("writeUsageError() error = %v, wantErr %v", err, tt.wantErr)
				}
				return
			}

			err := writeUsageError(w)
			if (err != nil) != tt.wantErr {
				t.Errorf("writeUsageError() error = %v, wantErr %v", err, tt.wantErr)
			}
		})
	}
}

// Re-implementing bytes.Buffer locally to avoid extra imports if needed, 
// but bytes is standard library, so we use it.
import "bytes"
```

Wait, I must ensure I follow the rules: "Every import must be used". I used `bytes` in the test but didn't declare it in the top imports. I'll fix the structure.

```go
package cli

import (
	"bytes"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"testing"
)

type writeUsageErrorWriterErr struct{}

func (w writeUsageErrorWriterErr) Write(p []byte) (n int, err error) {
	return 0, errors.New("write failed")
}

func TestWriteUsageError(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		writer  func() io.Writer
		wantErr bool
		errStr  string
	}{
		{
			name: "Happy path writes usage to writer",
			writer: func() io.Writer {
				return new(bytes.Buffer)
			},
			wantErr: false,
		},
		{
			name: "Returns error when writing to the writer fails",
			writer: func() io.Writer {
				return writeUsageErrorWriterErr{}
			},
			wantErr: true,
			errStr:  "write failed",
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			w := tt.writer()
			err := writeUsageError(w)
			if tt.wantErr {
				if err == nil {
					t.Fatal("expected error, got nil")
				}
				if err.Error() != tt.errStr {
					t.Errorf("expected error %q, got %q", tt.errStr, err.Error())
				}
			} else {
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
```
